{{Short description|19th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1949–50 National Hurling League |image = |caption = |dates = 1 October 1949 – 24 September 1950 |teams = 18 |team1 = Tipperary |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 3rd |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |previous = [[1948–49 National Hurling League|1948–49]] |next = [[1950–51 National Hurling League|1950–51]] }} The '''1949–50 National Hurling League''' was the 19th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==National Hurling League== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League]] | image = NHL Final 1950 programme.jpg | image_size = 250 |season=1949–50 |winners=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]
3rd National League title
Captain: [[Seán Kenny (hurler)|Seán Kenny]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 33 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1948–49 National Hurling League|1948–49]] |nextseason=[[1950–51 National Hurling League|1950–51]] |updated=19 March 2017 }} The National Hurling League saw a major restructuring for the 1949–50 season. Division 1 and Division 2 were combined to form one division of four groups. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1948–49 National Hurling League|1948–49 season]]. On 24 September 1950, Tipperary won the title after a 1–12 to 3–4 win over [[New York GAA|New York]] in the final.
